record.paper_title: Doubly-Special Relativity: First Results and Key Open Problems
record.original_question: How should the DSR program be extended from inertial observers and deformed special relativity to noninertial observers and a corresponding modification of general relativity? The paper states that no robust results had yet been obtained and emphasizes that the Planck scale may need to play a double role, both through the gravitational coupling linked to G and through the structure of spacetime or energy-momentum space. The open problem is to build a consistent general-relativistic extension of DSR that reconciles these two roles of the Planck scale.

evidence.quote: Of course, since the DSR research programme is considering a modification of Special Relativity, a natural next step to consider is the one in which an analogous modification is implemented at the level of General Relativity.
Nothing that can claim any robusteness has been obtained so far on this interesting point.

I believe that a key issue for such studies comes from the observation that we might be required to attribute to the Planck scale a double role: a role in the gravitational coupling (because of the relation between G and Ep) and a role in the structure of spacetime (energy-momentum space).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Doubly Special Relativity (DSR) is a deformation of special relativity in which, in addition to the speed of light c, a second observer-independent scale—the Planck energy E_p (equivalently the Planck length ℓ_p)—is introduced. Concretely, the Poincaré-invariant dispersion relation E^2 − p^2 c^2 = m^2 c^4 is replaced by a deformed relation of the form F(E, p; E_p) = m^2 c^4 whose form is preserved under a nonlinear (deformed) action of the Lorentz group on energy-momentum space, with E_p playing the role of an invariant scale.

The problem is to construct a consistent general-relativistic extension of DSR, that is, a theory that:

(a) reduces to ordinary general relativity in the limit E_p → ∞ (equivalently ℓ_p → 0 while keeping Newton's constant G fixed),
(b) reduces to flat-spacetime DSR in the limit G → 0 while keeping E_p (equivalently ℓ_p) fixed,
(c) provides a transformation law relating arbitrary, possibly noninertial, observers under which both c and E_p remain invariant,
(d) consistently reconciles the two distinct roles played by the Planck scale: its role in the gravitational coupling (through the relation G ∼ ℓ_p^2 in natural units) and its role in the deformed structure of spacetime or energy-momentum space (through the deformed dispersion relation and deformed Lorentz transformations).

Provide such a theory, or prove that no theory satisfying (a)–(d) can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent surveys on DSR (e.g., the 2010 review "Doubly-Special Relativity: Facts, Myths and Some Key Open Issues") and later work on "gravity's rainbow" and relative-locality frameworks treat the curved-spacetime/general-relativistic extension of DSR as still unresolved. Candidate frameworks (rainbow gravity, relative locality, κ-Poincaré-based curved-momentum-space models) exist, but no single, universally accepted general-relativistic extension reconciling the two roles of the Planck scale has been established. The problem is therefore still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Doubly-Special Relativity: Facts, Myths and Some Key Open Issues
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open issues in DSR including the lack of a definitive curved-spacetime/general-relativistic extension.
status_evidence.claim: The extension of DSR to curved spacetime (and to a deformed general relativity) remains an open issue.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to rainbow gravity / DSR curved spacetime
status_evidence.snippet: DSR is formulated as a deformation of flat-spacetime kinematics; its extension to curved spacetime is not unique and depends on which structures retain observer-independent meaning.
status_evidence.claim: No unique general-relativistic extension of DSR is known; multiple competing proposals exist.

status_evidence.title: Doubly special relativity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: DSR might be generalized towards a theory of quantum gravity which, extended up from the Planck scale, should deliver results indistinguishable from general relativity.
status_evidence.claim: A full general-relativistic generalization of DSR has not been completed.
